title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
why_read: A careful empirical study questioning whether chain-of-thought text actually reflects which reasoning steps matter, with direct implications for interpretability and process-reward-model research.
analysis: The authors operationalize 'importance' of a CoT step via Monte Carlo rollout advantage estimates and test whether LLM judges can identify truly important steps from the text alone, finding judges beat a baseline but fall well short of ceiling, especially for correct responses. This is a meaningful contribution to the ongoing debate about CoT faithfulness and legibility versus genuine interpretability, cautioning against over-trusting reasoning traces for supervision or auditing. It's methodologically solid and relevant to anyone building process reward models or relying on CoT for safety/interpretability claims.
